subject: Canary request: temporary routing waiver (no-fallback) for deterministic validation
messages:
From: Anna Castillo <anna@cloudmed.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-12T09:14:00-08:00
Subject: Request: pin model + disable fallback for validation canary

Hey Jordan,

We're ready to start the deterministic validation canary for CloudMed's clinical summarization flow next week. For the QA pass we need two things: a pinned model variant (redwood-3b-q8-std) and no automatic fallback routing for the duration of the test window so the outputs are repeatable across runs.

Can Redwood enable a temporary routing waiver (no-fallback) scoped to our org and the canary route for up to 72 hours in us-east-1? We'll ramp to 5% traffic and provide the test prompts; QA will be watching for regressions.

Attached is our short canary checklist. Let me know what info you need from your side.

Thanks,
Anna Castillo
Head of Integrations, CloudMed Solutions
attachments: canary_checklist.docx (referenced)

From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Anna Castillo <anna@cloudmed.com>
Date: 2026-12-12T10:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Request: pin model + disable fallback for validation canary

Looping product/infra/CS in — CloudMed is asking for a scoped no-fallback (routing waiver) and a pinned model variant for a 72-hour validation window. Important constraints: must be limited to their tenant + route, we need logging/tracing to capture any divergence, and a rollback path.

Can product confirm acceptability from a product/regression standpoint? Aditya, what operational changes are required to temporarily disable fallback for a single customer route? Monica — any customer comms concerns re SLA impact?

I'll coordinate approvals once we have risk notes and an ops playbook.

-Jordan
Jordan Blake
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-13T09:33:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Request: pin model + disable fallback for validation canary

Thanks for the ping. Product perspective: the request is reasonable for a short, scoped canary if we can guarantee observability and a fast fallback re-enable. A few asks before I can approve: 
- Exact start/end times (timezone) and SLO targets for the experiment (p95 latency, error budget).
- A test prompt set and expected output characteristics so we can run a pre-canary regression check.
- Confirmation that the pinned model variant is compatible with our security/quantization policy for tenant workloads.

Prefer we treat this as a conditional waiver: allow no-fallback but only if we have the KV cache isolation + request tracing enabled, and if infra can flip wafers back within 10 minutes.

I'll review the attached canary_plan_v2 once provided.

-Lauren
Lauren Bishop
Senior Product Manager, Routing & Policies

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-14T11:06:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Request: pin model + disable fallback for validation canary

Operational notes and feasibility: 
- We can implement a per-tenant routing override that disables automatic fallback for the specified route. It requires a short config change in the smart-router layer and a corresponding flag in the serving runtime to ignore model-fallback signals for that tenant/route.
- Risk: if the pinned variant has a silent regression or experiences memory pressure, requests will fail instead of delegating to a fallback model. We'll need a runbook and automated monitor to revert the override on error thresholds (5xx spike > 0.5% in 5m or p95 latency > 1.5x baseline).
- Timeline: 24h dev + test, 1h deployment window. Suggest a scoped window: 2026-12-15T09:00:00-08:00 to 2026-12-18T09:00:00-08:00 (48h to start, not 72h) — we want to reduce exposure.
- Attachments: canary_plan_v2.pdf (detailed steps), risk_matrix.xlsx (failure modes), routing-runbook-stub.md (rollback steps).

If product and CS are OK with 48h and the monitoring thresholds, we can schedule the change for 12/15 morning. We will also enable request-level tracing and prefix KV isolation for the route.

-Aditya
Aditya Rao
Infra: Serving Runtime

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-14T15:44:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Request: pin model + disable fallback for validation canary

CS perspective: CloudMed is comfortable with 48h, but they asked for 72h originally — they'll accept 48h if we offer a one-time 24h extension subject to risk sign-off. A few points: 
- We need a customer-facing brief that explains the exact scope and the rollback commitments (10min revert).
- If we do disable fallback, we should offer an increased monitoring cadence: twice-daily check-ins during the window and a post-canary quality review.
- SLA: disabling fallback increases chance of visible errors; legal needs to sign off on any temporary exceptions that could change perceived availability. I'll start an approval thread with our contracts team and attach a short customer brief template to the cloud drive link.

-Monica
Monica Patel
Customer Success Manager

From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Anna Castillo <anna@cloudmed.com>
Date: 2026-12-15T16:22:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Request: pin model + disable fallback for validation canary (final)

All — thanks for the quick turn. Summary and decision: 
- Approved: Scoped routing waiver (no-fallback) for CloudMed's canary, pinned to redwood-3b-q8-std, region: us-east-1, route: /v1/generate/clinical-summary.
- Window: 2026-12-15T09:00:00-08:00 to 2026-12-17T09:00:00-08:00 (48h).
- Conditions: KV cache isolation enabled, request-level tracing on, automated rollback thresholds (5xx > 0.5% in 5m OR p95 latency > 1.5x baseline), Infra will deploy and verify, Product will validate pre-canary regression, CS will confirm customer brief and legal sign-off.
- Next steps: Aditya to schedule deployment at 09:00 12/15 and post a brief in the runbook when complete. Lauren to confirm regression run by 18:00 12/14. Monica to share customer brief and legal contact. I will record the exception and send to leadership for visibility.

Anna — Jordan here: thanks for the flexibility on window. We'll run the 5% ramp and keep you updated. Please post the QA prompt set to the drive link and we'll confirm when we start.

-Jordan
Jordan Blake
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
